messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran a focused microbatch-size sweep this morning to compare streaming chat (server-streaming) vs non-streaming completions after the kernel-selector change. Seeing an unexpected p99.9 tail regression for streaming at small mb sizes (<=8).

priya: ugh, thanks for catching. can you drop the numbers and a short repro?

alex: quick paste from the sweep (avg seq len ~128, clients=500):
```
# chat-stream (streaming)
mb=4   p50=18ms  p95=78ms  p99=180ms  p99.9=420ms  throughput=320 req/s
mb=8   p50=20ms  p95=82ms  p99=190ms  p99.9=230ms  throughput=580 req/s
mb=16  p50=25ms  p95=95ms  p99=210ms  p99.9=240ms  throughput=1100 req/s

# non-stream completions (sync)
mb=4   p99.9=120ms
mb=16  p99.9=150ms
```
Observations: small streaming batches show large p99.9 spikes vs sync. Tracing shows frequent kernel-selector churn during handshake -> kernel fallback to the FP32 path + KV-cache eviction spikes around the same time.

chao: is this linked to the kernel-fallback change from yesterday (commit a2c)? I remember adding a safety fallback for short sequences.

alex: yes, exactly. sprof around the spike shows repeated select/fallback cycles: kernel_select -> run_fp16 -> fallback_run_fp32 -> reselect. That oscillation aligns with handshake timing for stream responses. Also saw `kvcache.evict_rate +14%` in metrics during those windows.

sam: can you share the repro script and upload nvprof traces? I can run a GPU-level flamegraph.

alex: repro: `./scripts/mb_sweep_stream_vs_sync --clients=500 --seq-dist=zipf(1.2) --streaming=true` output + traces uploaded to perf-board ticket #4321 (link: https://perf-board/issue/4321). nvprof attached there.

priya: quick mitigation ideas: 1) increase kernel-selection hysteresis for streaming handshake so we don't oscillate on tiny timing variations, 2) bias chooser to prefer the fast FP16 path when sequence len variance is low, 3) add small randomized jitter to selection timings to avoid lockstep between clients.

alex: tried a 120ms hysteresis in a local run: mb=4 p99.9 dropped 420ms -> 210ms, throughput dropped ~8%. So tradeoff is median/throughput vs extreme tail.

infra-bot: deploy:kernel-selector-v2 reverted to v1 at 08:22 UTC (reason: p99 regressions observed in canary).

jon: can we also reduce kvcache churn? maybe adaptive prefetch / pin hot prefixes for clients with high sequence variance. Evictions are amplifying the tail because KV misses incur additional kernel work.

chao: +1 on adaptive prefetch. Also think adding a tiny jitter (10-20ms) to kernel-selection decisions prevents multiple clients from hitting the fallback simultaneously. That should reduce eviction spikes.

alex: plan for next canary: (1) hysteresis=120ms + jitter=15ms for kernel selector, (2) kvcache: pin top-100 hot prefixes for canary clients, (3) collect sprof/nvprof & p99/p99.9 histograms for both streaming and sync. I'll open a CL and schedule the canary.

priya: sounds good. i'll watch the SLO dashboard and alert rules. ping me when it's live. :eyes:

alex: will do. thanks all — i'll post the canary link and initial histograms here once available. :thumbsup:
